brief.topic: W8 challenge v3: DeepSeek Harness plugin ecosystem and composable capability supply

criteria.question: What is each project's exact identity, owner, purpose, users, and relationship to DeepSeek Harness; distinguish official components, DSH plugins, ecosystem registries, bridges, and unrelated outer runtimes?
What source or documentation proves a plugin, extension, package, MCP, ACP, hook, skill, provider, or protocol contract; how are discovery, loading, configuration, versioning, and lifecycle handled?

Which ZWorkbench capability does the project supply or extend: automation/scheduling, durable state, interruption/recovery, provider routing/failover, observability/replay/evaluation, sandbox/approval, code workflow, or operations/exit?
What state, identity, event, effect, retry, approval, replay, and failure semantics are actually implemented; can the capability map to the W6 C1-C7 contract without inventing ownership?
What integration seam exists for an outer composition owner: API/CLI/ACP/MCP/event stream/database/SDK; what translation, duplicate state, or single-owner conflict would integration create?
What security, sandbox, credentials, network, external side effect, remote data, webhook, deployment, backup, and exit assumptions are disclosed; which boundaries remain unknown?
What license, governance, release/version, dependency, compatibility, maintenance, and source-to-binary provenance signals exist; keep stars/popularity separate from capability evidence?

What ownership responsibilities, permanent services, upgrade matrix, migration, troubleshooting, and exit work would a personal developer or small team inherit when composing this project with DeepSeek Harness?
